name: African Violet
hook: African violet not blooming? It needs more light.

steps.title: Bright, cool light
steps.tip: A north or east window, out of strong summer sun. To flower, it needs 14–16 hrs of light and 8 hrs dark.

steps.title: Water the soil, not leaves
steps.tip: Use room-temperature water on the mix or from below. Drops on leaves leave spots. Never let it sit in water.

steps.title: Steady 16–24°C
steps.tip: Aim for 18–24°C by day and about 16°C at night, away from cold drafts and sudden changes.

steps.title: Humid air, dry leaves
steps.tip: Stand the pot on a tray of damp gravel, above the water. Don't mist: it marks leaves and invites mould.

steps.title: Feed it lightly
steps.tip: Dilute African violet or houseplant feed every 3–4 weeks in spring and summer.

steps.title: Keep the pot small
steps.tip: Repot in spring every 2–3 years, into a pot only slightly bigger than the roots, usually 10 cm across.

outro: Bright light, dry leaves and a snug pot keep violets in bloom.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension: Growing African violets
RHS: How to grow African violets

faqs.question: Why are there pale spots on the leaves?
faqs.answer: Water left sitting on the leaves causes spots. Water the mix directly or from below with room-temperature water.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension: Growing African violets
